purpose: Source research and publication audit. Only IDs in publication are imported. Event candidates may represent multiple dates and unresolved details; do not import them wholesale.

organizations.name: Alliance San Diego
organizations.description: Alliance San Diego brings neighbors together to build community power and protect human dignity. Its work combines civic education, leadership development, human-rights advocacy, and immigration legal assistance.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Virtual civic training on October 6, 7, 27 and 28. September 30 public-charge webinars also advertised on the homepage; end times need confirmation.

organizations.name: San Diego Organizing Project
organizations.description: A multifaith network that helps San Diego County residents organize around shared concerns. Its campaigns address housing, immigration, justice-system reform, and public accountability through community leadership and collective action.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Reviewed the calendar and its linked public Google Calendar feed. No future entries found in the review window; some listed organizing meetings are not open to the public.

organizations.name: Pathways to Citizenship
organizations.description: Pathways helps immigrant families navigate citizenship and other immigration processes through legal assistance and education. Its San Diego County programs include citizenship-test preparation and opportunities for community members to volunteer as tutors.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Party with a Purpose: October 4, 3 p.m. until sunset. Venue, ticket details and a precise end time need confirmation.

organizations.name: San Diego World Affairs Council
organizations.description: A nonpartisan forum connecting San Diegans with global issues through speakers, discussions, and educational programs. Topics include diplomacy, migration, international security, and the relationships between local communities and the wider world.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Three detailed listings checked: October 1, October 10 and November 14. See the event table.
organizations.organizationType: Local organization affiliated with a national council network

organizations.name: House of Palestine
organizations.description: Located among Balboa Park’s International Cottages, House of Palestine shares Palestinian history and culture through exhibits, food, dance, workshops, and community gatherings. Volunteers help visitors connect with Palestinian heritage and everyday life.
organizations.eventReviewNote: The El-Funoun series ends September 25, with a theater presentation at 6 p.m.; keep it separate from the future window. Weekend house hosting is advertised from 11 a.m. No later dated special event verified.
organizations.editorialNote: Member of House of Pacific Relations; do not duplicate shared events.

organizations.name: KARAMA
organizations.description: KARAMA promotes understanding of the Arab and Islamic worlds, with particular attention to Palestinian experiences. Its cultural and educational work includes the San Diego Arab Film Festival, which shares stories from and about Arab communities.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Two October 24 films announced: El Sett and Who Killed Alex Odeh? Venue confirmed; showtimes need checking.
organizations.editorialNote: Main KARAMA site had an expired-certificate error. Its official film-festival site was accessible and identifies the festival as a KARAMA project.

organizations.name: Islamic Center of San Diego
organizations.description: A mosque and community center offering religious services, education, youth activities, and support for families. Its programs create opportunities for learning, volunteering, and connection within San Diego’s Muslim community.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Homepage and public calendar list ongoing classes, lectures and community programs. Record these as recurring opportunities; confirm current session timing before generating individual dates.

organizations.name: Partnership for the Advancement of New Americans (PANA)
organizations.description: PANA is a refugee-founded and refugee-led organization building belonging and civic power. It supports community leadership, policy advocacy, and storytelling so refugee and immigrant communities can shape the decisions that affect their lives.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Global Village/PANA Event Hall is a vote center October 24–November 3. PANA’s published hours conflict with the Registrar’s; use the official county schedule and address recorded below.

organizations.name: JUST Education Collective
organizations.description: A women-owned grassroots collective supporting families, students, caregivers, and educators across San Diego County. Through mutual aid, resource sharing, storytelling, and advocacy, it helps communities respond to inequity in K–12 education.
organizations.eventReviewNote: The page labels November 16 and December 7 events as upcoming but gives no year. Sunday November 16 aligns with 2025, not 2026, and adjacent entries explicitly reference 2025. Do not import as 2026 events.
organizations.editorialNote: Kasey’s group is this organization; keep one profile.

organizations.name: Border Angels
organizations.description: Border Angels supports migrants and refugees through humanitarian aid, education, and advocacy in the U.S.–Mexico border region. Its programs include desert water drops, assistance to migrant shelters, and outreach to day laborers.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Monthly water drops and Caravan of Love are described publicly, but individual dates and logistics are shared through approved volunteer registration. No dates inferred.
organizations.organizationType: San Diego-based organization working across the border region

organizations.name: Kind Hearts San Diego
organizations.description: Kind Hearts welcomes refugees and newcomers through practical assistance, donated resources, and community support. Based in La Mesa, it brings volunteers together to help families build connections and settle into life in San Diego.
organizations.eventReviewNote: The events page lists a 2025 newcomers blanket drive and an emergency food drive, both with date/time and location TBD. No calendar-ready event found.

organizations.name: San Diego International Sister Cities Association
organizations.description: San Diego’s sister-city umbrella association supports connections with communities around the world. It brings together local societies working on cultural, educational, economic, and humanitarian exchanges that encourage understanding and peace.
organizations.eventReviewNote: The embedded calendar did not expose a readable schedule. A current news post announces a House of Panama sweepstakes drawing on October 3, but no start time; this is a partner fundraiser, not a verified SanDISCA-hosted public gathering.

organizations.name: House of Pacific Relations International Cottages
organizations.description: The International Cottages in Balboa Park bring together cultural houses representing communities from around the world. Open houses and lawn programs invite visitors to discover food, music, dance, history, and traditions through local volunteers.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Ten lawn-program dates listed between September 26 and November 15. The first four also have explicit 11 a.m.–4 p.m. homepage listings; later dates use the annual program’s general timing guidance.

organizations.name: San Diego Refugee Communities Coalition
organizations.description: A coalition of community-based organizations supporting refugee communities across San Diego County. Members coordinate work on health, housing, economic opportunity, and other priorities, centering the knowledge and leadership of the communities they serve.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Reviewed homepage and news. The latest event story reports an April 4, 2026 town hall, posted in August; it is not an upcoming event. No future dated public event found.

organizations.name: CAIR California — San Diego
organizations.description: CAIR’s San Diego office supports civil rights, immigrant communities, and civic participation. Its work includes responding to discrimination, providing legal assistance, and offering education and advocacy opportunities for local communities.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Beyond the Headlines conference: October 16, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. on the official event page. Venue and admission need confirmation; the linked ticket site blocked automated access.
organizations.organizationType: San Diego office of a larger organization

organizations.name: Jewish Voice for Peace San Diego
organizations.description: The San Diego chapter of Jewish Voice for Peace brings together anti-Zionist Jews and allies advocating for Palestinian freedom and equal rights. It offers ways to learn, build community, and participate in collective advocacy.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Event page says no upcoming signups. Its public Google Calendar had no dates in the review window; the most recent September event found was September 13.
organizations.organizationType: Local chapter of a national advocacy organization

organizations.name: Palestine Children’s Relief Fund — San Diego
organizations.description: PCRF’s San Diego chapter connects local volunteers with efforts to support children’s medical care and humanitarian needs in Palestine and the wider region. Chapters raise awareness and funds and help support children receiving treatment.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Seeds of Healing benefit dinner is listed for October 17 at Four Point Sheraton. The index says 5:00 am Pacific Time (PST), inconsistent with a dinner; do not silently change it to p.m. The linked registration page requires dynamic rendering.
organizations.organizationType: Local chapter of an international charity

organizations.name: International Rescue Committee in San Diego
organizations.description: IRC’s San Diego office helps refugees, asylum seekers, and other immigrants rebuild their lives. Local programs support employment, education, youth, wellbeing, small-business development, and access to immigration legal services.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Taste of the IRC: October 29, doors 6:15 p.m., start 6:30 p.m., Building 177 at Liberty Station. End time and current ticket price need checking.
organizations.organizationType: San Diego office of an international organization

organizations.name: HEAL Palestine
organizations.description: HEAL Palestine supports Palestinian children and communities through healthcare, education, humanitarian aid, and leadership programs. San Diego supporters have participated in local fundraising, connecting community action here with assistance abroad.
organizations.eventReviewNote: The current upcoming-events list names Virginia, North Carolina and Florida events, but no San Diego date. Do not import other cities’ events into the local calendar.
organizations.organizationType: Broader humanitarian organization with San Diego activity
organizations.editorialNote: User confirmed identity; do not imply an independently verified formal San Diego chapter.

organizations.name: The Humanization Matters Collaborative
organizations.description: The Humanization Matters Collaborative works to counter dehumanization and center the voices of oppressed and Indigenous communities. It offers advisory work, community partnerships, and research focused on dignity and equity in healthcare, education, and media.
organizations.eventReviewNote: No dated public events found on the reviewed site pages. Speaking requests and advisory services are offered, but they are not scheduled public events.
organizations.organizationType: San Diego-run organization; location confirmed firsthand by site owner
organizations.editorialNote: New organization and San Diego operation confirmed by user. HTTPS certificate error remains; identity/profile content was inspected separately from normal secure access.

organizations.name: Activist San Diego
organizations.description: Activist San Diego connects people and organizations working for social justice through community organizing, education, and media. Its public community calendar helps residents discover local gatherings and opportunities to get involved.
organizations.eventReviewNote: The public calendar contains dated community events, including September 30 actions. Many are hosted by other groups: treat Activist San Diego as the source, not automatically the organizer. Its own summit post is dated March 16, 2026; do not generate future summits solely from the usual monthly pattern.

organizations.name: Media Arts Center San Diego
organizations.description: Media Arts Center San Diego expands access to filmmaking, creative learning, and community storytelling. Its programs include youth media education, Digital Gym Cinema, and the San Diego Latino Film Festival, creating space for underrepresented voices and shared cultural experiences.
organizations.eventReviewNote: Digital Gym screenings include The Great Experiment with filmmaker Q&A on October 23 and The Proposition on November 22. November 23–25 youth camp is also advertised; daily times and price need checking.
organizations.editorialNote: Digital Gym Cinema is a program/venue, not a second organization profile. November workforce-program applications are an opportunity, not a dated public event.

organizations.name: San Diego Foundation
organizations.description: San Diego Foundation connects charitable giving with community priorities across San Diego County. Through grants, scholarships, and partnerships with local nonprofits, it supports education, children and families, the environment, and opportunities for communities to thrive.
organizations.eventReviewNote: The official events page lists the October 7, 2026 Professional Advisor Symposium and an October 2026 Fifty & Forward Closing Celebration as invitation-only. The symposium save-the-date gives 12:30–5:30 p.m. PT at Farmer & The Seahorse, Americana Room. Do not present either as an open public event. The next fundraising conference listed is September 14–15, 2027, outside this review window.
organizations.editorialNote: San Diego-based, but a major regional foundation rather than a small business. Included at the user’s explicit request. Grants and scholarships belong under resources/opportunities rather than being turned into calendar events.
